description: The clear dome at the very front of the eye. It bends most of the light that enters the eye. (Prototype description.)
The colored ring of muscle that changes the size of the pupil to let in more or less light. (Prototype description.)
A clear, flexible disc behind the iris. It changes shape to focus on things that are near or far. (Prototype description.)
Tiny fibers that hold the lens in place and let it change shape. (Prototype description.)
The tough white outer wall of the eye. It protects the eye and helps it keep its shape. (Prototype description.)
The dark middle layer under the sclera. It is rich in blood vessels that feed the retina. (Prototype description.)
The light-sensitive lining at the back of the eye. It turns light into signals for the brain. (Prototype description.)
The cable of nerve fibers that carries signals from the retina to the brain. (Prototype description.)
